items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: as were Lennon McCartney and Ringo and Harrison, as far as they were listening to that stuff and then creating a British version of it.

ctx.x: Do you listen, do you recall listening for the bass notes?

Oh totally. I listened to all the parts. We had Radio Luxembourg, was, you know, broadcast from the continent, so it wasn’t restricted to the same playlists that the BBC had, which was, at that time, we didn’t have Radio One, Radio Two until somewhat later. 1963, ’64 it was The Light Program or The Home Service or whatever. So you got a very eclectic mix there anyway. But Radio Luxembourg was all-American top 40. So that’s where I heard all those records. I heard Motown Records for the first time. And I’d be ©…

listening to what the rhythm section was doing, and how the bass and the kick drum work together, as were Lennon McCartney and Ringo and Harrison, as far as they were listening to that stuff and then creating a British version of it. In fact the first time a Motown song was ever played on British radio was by The Beatles in 1962. I forget which song it was. But it was a live broadcast and they played a Motown song. Because you didn’t hear that, and then you did. Then all of a sudden you started to hear that…
